title.en: Volume 33 Biographies 14: Wang Sengqian, Zhang Xu

sentences.zh: 南齊書卷三十三‧列傳第十四

translations.literal: Book of the Southern Qi, Volume 33 — Biography 14
translations.idiomatic: Book of the Southern Qi, Volume 33 — Biography 14

sentences.zh: 王僧虔 張緒

translations.literal: Wang Sengqian; Zhang Xu
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sengqian; Zhang Xu

sentences.zh: 王僧虔，琅邪臨沂人也。

translations.literal: Wang Sengqian was a native of Linyi in Langye.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sengqian was a man of Linyi in Langye.

sentences.zh: 祖珣，晉司徒。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xun was grand steward of the Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xun had been grand steward under the Jin.

sentences.zh: 伯父太保弘，宋元嘉世爲宰輔。

translations.literal: His father's elder brother, Grand Tutor Hong, in the Yuanjia era of Liu Song served as chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: His father's elder brother, Grand Tutor Hong, in Liu Song's Yuanjia reign had served as chief minister.

sentences.zh: 賔客疑所諱，弘曰：「身家諱與蘇子高同。

translations.literal: Guests doubted which taboo names to use; Hong said: 「The taboo of my person and household is the same as Su Zigao's.
translations.idiomatic: Guests were unsure which names to avoid; Hong said: 「The taboo of my person and household is the same as Su Zigao's.

sentences.zh: 」父曇首，右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: 」His father Tanshou was right grand master for luminous offerings.
translations.idiomatic: 」His father Tanshou was right grand master for luminous offerings.

sentences.zh: 曇首兄弟集會諸子孫，弘子僧達下地跳戲，僧虔年數歲，獨正坐採蠟燭珠爲鳳凰。

translations.literal: When Tanshou's brothers gathered their sons and grandsons, Hong's son Sengda leapt down to play, while Sengqian, only a few years old, sat upright alone fashioning a phoenix from wax-candle beads.
translations.idiomatic: When Tanshou's brothers gathered their sons and grandsons, Hong's son Sengda leapt down to romp, while Sengqian, only a few years old, sat upright alone shaping a phoenix from wax-candle beads.

sentences.zh: 弘曰：「此兒終當爲長者。」

translations.literal: Hong said: 「This boy will surely become an elder in the end.」
translations.idiomatic: Hong said: 「This boy will surely become the clan's elder one day.」

sentences.zh: 僧虔弱冠，弘厚，善隷書。

translations.literal: At his weak-crown year Sengqian had a stout build and was skilled at clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: Coming of age, Sengqian was thickset and excelled at clerical script.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝見其書素扇，歎曰：「非唯迹逾子敬，方當器雅過之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Song saw his writing on a plain fan and exclaimed: 「Not only do his traces surpass Zijing's—his refined bearing will surely surpass him as well.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Song saw his writing on a plain fan and sighed: 「Not only do his strokes surpass Zijing's—his refined bearing will soon outshine him as well.

sentences.zh: 」除祕書郎，太子舍人。

translations.literal: 」He was appointed secretary gentleman and aide to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: 」He was named secretary gentleman and aide to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 退默少交接，與袁淑、謝莊善。

translations.literal: Reserved and reticent, he had few social ties; he was on good terms with Yuan Shu and Xie Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Withdrawn and sparing in company, he kept few ties abroad; he was close to Yuan Shu and Xie Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 轉義陽王文學，太子洗馬，遷司徒左西屬。

translations.literal: He was transferred to literary aide to Prince of Yiyang, wash for the crown prince, and moved to left western aide to the grand steward.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to literary aide to Prince of Yiyang, wash for the crown prince, then to left western aide on the grand steward's staff.

sentences.zh: 兄僧綽，爲太初所害，親賔咸勸僧虔逃。

translations.literal: His elder brother Sengchuo was killed in the Taichu turmoil; relatives and guests all urged Sengqian to flee.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Sengchuo was slain in the Taichu reign; kin and guests alike urged Sengqian to flee.

sentences.zh: 僧虔涕泣曰：「吾兄奉國以忠貞，撫我以慈愛，今日之事，苦不見及耳。

translations.literal: Sengqian wept and said: 「My brother served the state with loyalty and nurtured me with kindness—in today's affair, I bitterly regret that I did not share his fate.
translations.idiomatic: Sengqian wept and said: 「My brother served the state with loyalty and raised me with kindness—in what has happened today, I bitterly wish I had not been spared.

sentences.zh: 若同歸九泉，猶羽化也。

translations.literal: If we could go together to the nine springs, it would still be like shedding the mortal shell.
translations.idiomatic: If we could go together to the nine springs, it would still be like shedding the mortal shell.

sentences.zh: 」孝武初，出爲武陵太守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu he went out as administrator of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Emperor Xiaowu's reign he went out as administrator of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 兄子儉於中途得病，僧虔爲廢寢食。

translations.literal: His brother's son Jian fell ill on the road midway; Sengqian forwent sleep and food for it.
translations.idiomatic: His brother's son Jian took ill on the road midway; Sengqian gave up sleep and meals for his sake.

sentences.zh: 同行客慰喻之。

translations.literal: Fellow travelers on the road comforted and exhorted him.
translations.idiomatic: Fellow travelers on the road comforted and urged him on.

sentences.zh: 僧虔曰：「昔馬援處兒姪之閒一情不異，鄧攸於弟子更逾所生，吾實懷其心，誠未異古。

translations.literal: Sengqian said: 「In olden days Ma Yuan treated sons and nephews with one undivided feeling; Deng You toward his younger brother's son went even beyond what he owed his own issue—I truly hold that heart in me and am in no way unlike the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: Sengqian said: 「Long ago Ma Yuan made no distinction of feeling between sons and nephews; Deng You toward his brother's son went even beyond what he owed his own children—I hold that same heart and am in no way unlike the ancients.

sentences.zh: 亡兄之胤，不宜忽諸。

translations.literal: My dead brother's heir ought not to be cast aside.
translations.idiomatic: My dead brother's heir must not be cast aside.

sentences.zh: 若此兒不救，便當回舟謝職，無復遊宦之興矣。

translations.literal: If this boy is not saved, I shall turn the boat back and resign my post; I will have no further taste for office-seeking travel.
translations.idiomatic: If this boy cannot be saved, I shall turn the boat back and resign my post; I will have no further heart for roaming in office.

sentences.zh: 」還爲中書郎，轉黃門郎，太子中庶子。

translations.literal: 」He returned and became gentleman of the secretariat, then gentleman of the yellow gate and junior mentor to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: 」He returned and became gentleman of the secretariat, then gentleman of the yellow gate and junior mentor to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 孝武欲擅書名，僧虔不敢顯迹。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu wished to monopolize the fame of calligraphy; Sengqian did not dare display his traces openly.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu wished to keep the fame of calligraphy to himself; Sengqian did not dare show his hand openly.

sentences.zh: 大明世，常用掘筆書，以此見容。

translations.literal: In the Daming era he commonly used a blunt brush to write, and by this was tolerated.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daming era he commonly wrote with a stub brush, and by that was spared.

sentences.zh: 出爲豫章王子尚撫軍長史，遷散騎常侍，復爲新安王子鸞北中郎長史、南東海太守，行南徐州事，二蕃皆帝愛子也。

translations.literal: He went out as chief clerk on Prince of Yuzhang Zishang's pacification staff, moved to attendant at leisure, then again became chief clerk on Prince of Xin'an Ziluan's northern central commandant staff and administrator of Southern Donghai, with charge of southern Xuzhou affairs—both feudatories were the emperor's beloved sons.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as chief clerk on Prince of Yuzhang Zishang's pacification staff, was moved to attendant at leisure, then again became chief clerk on Prince of Xin'an Ziluan's northern central commandant staff and administrator of Southern Donghai, with charge of southern Xuzhou—both posts were the emperor's beloved sons.

sentences.zh: 尋遷豫章內史。

translations.literal: Before long he was moved to interior administrator of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was moved to interior administrator of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 入爲侍中，遷御史中丞，領驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: He entered the court as palace attendant, moved to director of the censorate, and also led the fierce-cavalry general.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as palace attendant, was moved to director of the censorate, and also led the fierce-cavalry general.

sentences.zh: 甲族向來多不居憲臺，王氏以分枝居烏衣者，位官微減，僧虔爲此官，乃曰：「此是烏衣諸郎坐處，我亦可試爲耳。

translations.literal: Leading clans had long seldom held the censor's bench; among the Wang clan, the branch that dwelt on Wuyi Lane saw their offices slightly reduced—when Sengqian took this post he said: 「This is where the gentlemen of Wuyi Lane sit; I too may try it for a while.
translations.idiomatic: Great clans had long shunned the censor's bench; among the Wangs, the branch that lived on Wuyi Lane had seen their offices slightly diminished—when Sengqian took the post he said: 「This is where the gentlemen of Wuyi Lane sit; I too may try it awhile.

sentences.zh: 」復爲侍中，領屯騎校尉。

translations.literal: 」He was again palace attendant and also led the colonel of the encampment cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: 」He was again palace attendant and also led the colonel of the encampment cavalry.

sentences.zh: 泰始中，出爲輔國將軍、吳興太守，秩中二千石。

translations.literal: In the Taishi era he went out as general who assists the state and administrator of Wuxing, stipend at middle-two-thousand-dan rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taishi era he went out as general who assists the state and administrator of Wuxing, with stipend at middle two-thousand-dan rank.

sentences.zh: 王獻之善書，爲吳興郡，及僧虔工書，又爲郡，論者稱之。

translations.literal: Wang Xianzhi was skilled at calligraphy and held Wu commandery; now Sengqian too excelled at calligraphy and again held the commandery—talkers paired their names.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xianzhi was skilled at calligraphy and had held Wu commandery; when Sengqian too mastered the brush and again held the commandery, talkers paired their names.

sentences.zh: 徙爲會稽太守，秩中二千石，將軍如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to administrator of Kuaiji, stipend at middle-two-thousand-dan rank, general as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to administrator of Kuaiji, stipend at middle two-thousand-dan rank, his generalship unchanged.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人阮佃夫家在會稽，請假東歸。

translations.literal: Palace Interior Retainer Ruan Tianfu's family was in Kuaiji; he asked leave to travel east and return home.
translations.idiomatic: Palace interior retainer Ruan Tianfu's family was in Kuaiji; he asked leave to travel east and return home.

sentences.zh: 客勸僧虔以佃夫要倖，宜加禮接。

translations.literal: Guests urged Sengqian that Tianfu enjoyed the emperor's favor and that he ought to show him extra courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Guests urged Sengqian that Tianfu stood in the emperor's favor and that he ought to treat him with added ceremony.

sentences.zh: 僧虔曰：「我立身有素，豈能曲意此輩。

translations.literal: Sengqian said: 「I have long stood on my own footing—how could I bend my intentions to such people?
translations.idiomatic: Sengqian said: 「I have long stood on my own footing—how could I bend my will to such people?

sentences.zh: 彼若見惡，當拂衣去耳。

translations.literal: If they come to hate me for it, I shall only shake out my robes and leave.
translations.idiomatic: If they take offense, I shall only shake out my robes and go.

sentences.zh: 」佃夫言於宋明帝，使御史中丞孫敻奏：「僧虔前莅吳興，多有謬命，檢到郡至遷，凡用功曹五官主簿至二禮吏署三傳及度與弟子，合四百四十八人。

translations.literal: 」Tianfu spoke to Emperor Ming of Song, and had the censorate director Sun Que impeach him: 「Sengqian, when he previously governed Wuxing, issued many wrongful appointments; from arrival at the commandery until his transfer, in all he employed from merit clerks and five-offices chief recorders through the two-rites clerks' office transmission students and quota disciples—448 persons in total.
translations.idiomatic: 」Tianfu spoke to Emperor Ming of Song and had censorate director Sun Que impeach him: 「When Sengqian previously governed Wuxing he issued many wrongful appointments; from his arrival until his transfer, in all he placed merit clerks, five-offices chief recorders, two-rites clerks' transmission students, and quota disciples—448 persons in total.

sentences.zh: 又聽民何係先等一百十家爲舊門。

translations.literal: He also allowed the commoner He Xixian and 110 households to be registered as old eminent families.
translations.idiomatic: He also allowed the commoner He Xixian and 110 households to be registered as old eminent families.

sentences.zh: 委州檢削。

translations.literal: Refer the matter to the province for verification and reduction.
translations.idiomatic: Refer the matter to the province for verification and reduction.

sentences.zh: 」坐免官。

translations.literal: He was convicted and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He was convicted and removed from office.

sentences.zh: 尋以白衣兼侍中，出監吳郡太守，遷使持節、都督湘州諸軍事、建武將軍、行湘州事，仍轉輔國將軍，湘州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long, in plain clothes he concurrently served as palace attendant, went out to supervise the administrator of Wu commandery, was moved to bearer of the staff as supervisor of military affairs for Xiang province, general who establishes might, with charge of Xiang affairs, then transferred to general who assists the state and inspector of Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, in plain dress he concurrently served as palace attendant, went out to supervise the administrator of Wu commandery, was moved to bearer of the staff as supervisor of military affairs for Xiang, general who establishes might, with charge of Xiang affairs, then to general who assists the state and inspector of Xiang.

sentences.zh: 所在以寬惠著稱。

translations.literal: In every place he was known for lenience and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: In every post he was known for lenience and kindness.

sentences.zh: 巴峽流民多在湘土，僧虔表割益陽、羅、湘西三縣緣江民立湘陰縣，從之。

translations.literal: Displaced people from Ba Gorge were many in Xiang lands; Sengqian memorialized to carve from Yiyang, Luo, and Xiangxi the three counties' river-bank commoners to establish Xiangyin county—the emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: Displaced people from Ba Gorge were numerous in Xiang territory; Sengqian memorialized to cut from Yiyang, Luo, and Xiangxi the river-bank households of three counties and establish Xiangyin county—the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 元徽中，遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhui era he was moved to director of the ministry of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanhui era he was moved to director of the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 高平檀珪罷沅南令，僧虔以爲征北板行參軍。

translations.literal: Tan Gui of Gaoping had left office as administrator of Yuannan; Sengqian made him eastern-strike staff acting aide.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Gui of Gaoping had left office as administrator of Yuannan; Sengqian made him acting aide on the eastern-strike staff.

sentences.zh: 訴僧虔求祿不得，與僧虔書曰：「五常之始，文武爲先，文則經緯天地，武則撥亂定國。

translations.literal: Gui complained that Sengqian would not grant him salary and wrote to Sengqian: 「At the start of the five constants, wen and wu come first—wen threads heaven and earth together, wu quells disorder and settles the state.
translations.idiomatic: Gui complained that Sengqian would not grant him salary and wrote to him: 「At the founding of the five constants, wen and wu stand foremost—wen threads heaven and earth together; wu quells disorder and settles the realm.

sentences.zh: 僕一門雖謝文通，乃忝武達。

translations.literal: Though my household may have declined in literary attainment, we are not unworthy in martial eminence.
translations.idiomatic: Though my household may have fallen short in literary attainment, we are not unworthy in martial eminence.

sentences.zh: 羣從姑叔，三媾帝室，祖兄二世，糜軀奉國，而致子姪餓死草壤。

translations.literal: Among the clan's paternal uncles, three marriages joined the imperial house; grandfather and elder brother for two generations gave their bodies to serve the state, yet it brought sons and nephews to starve and die on the open field.
translations.idiomatic: Among the clan's paternal uncles, three marriages joined the imperial house; grandfather and elder brother for two generations gave their flesh to serve the state—yet it brought sons and nephews to starve and die on the open field.

sentences.zh: 去冬今春，頻荷二敕，旣無中人，屢見蹉奪。

translations.literal: Last winter and this spring, repeatedly I received two edicts; yet with no go-between, time and again my appointments were snatched away.
translations.idiomatic: Last winter and again this spring I received two imperial edicts, yet without a broker at court my appointments were seized again and again.

sentences.zh: 經涉五朔，踰歷四晦，書牘十二，接覲六七，遂不荷潤，反更曝鰓。

translations.literal: Through five first days of the month, spanning four month-ends, twelve letters, audiences six or seven — in the end I received no favor, but instead was further dried with gills exposed.
translations.idiomatic: Five months and four month-ends have passed; I have sent twelve letters and gained six or seven audiences — yet no kindness came, and I am left more destitute than before.

sentences.zh: 九流繩平，自不宜獨苦一物，蟬腹龜腸，爲日已久。

translations.literal: The nine streams are leveled by the cord — alone one thing should not be made to suffer; cicada belly and tortoise gut have been so for many days.
translations.idiomatic: When all walks of life are judged by one measure, a single man should not bear the whole burden; I have been hollow with hunger for a very long time.

sentences.zh: 飢虎能嚇，人遽與肉；

translations.literal: A hungry tiger can frighten — men at once give it meat;
translations.idiomatic: A starving tiger only has to snarl and men rush to feed it meat;

sentences.zh: 餓麟不噬，誰爲落毛。

translations.literal: A starving qilin does not bite — who will pluck its feathers for it?
translations.idiomatic: a starving qilin will not bite, and no one will even pluck its fallen feathers.

sentences.zh: 去冬乞豫章丞，爲馬超所爭；

translations.literal: Last winter I begged for Yuzhang assistant magistrate — it was contested by Ma Chao;
translations.idiomatic: Last winter I asked for the assistant magistracy of Yuzhang and lost the post to Ma Chao;

sentences.zh: 今春蒙敕南昌縣，爲史偃所奪。

translations.literal: This spring I received an edict for Nanchang county — it was seized by Shi Yan.
translations.idiomatic: this spring I was granted Nanchang county magistrate and had it taken by Shi Yan.

sentences.zh: 二子勳蔭人才，有何見勝。

translations.literal: The two men's merit-shade and talent — what superiority do they show?
translations.idiomatic: Those two men inherit merit and office — in what way are they my betters?

sentences.zh: 若以貧富相奪，則分受不如。

translations.literal: If by rich and poor one seizes posts, then in allotment of shares I am the worse.
translations.idiomatic: If posts are handed out according to wealth and poverty, then by rights of inheritance I am the poorer man.

sentences.zh: 身雖孤微，百世國士，姻媾位宦，亦不後物。

translations.literal: Though my person is solitary and slight, for a hundred generations a house of state gentlemen; marriage ties and rank and office, I am not behind others.
translations.idiomatic: Humble as I am, my house for generations has produced men who served the state; in marriage alliances and official standing I am not beneath others.

sentences.zh: 尚書同堂姊爲江夏王妃，檀珪同堂姑爲南譙王妃；

translations.literal: The Minister's cousin by the same grandfather was Princess of Jiangxia; Tan Gui's cousin by the same grandfather was Princess of Nanqiao;
translations.idiomatic: Your paternal cousin by marriage was Princess of Jiangxia; my own paternal aunt held the same rank as Princess of Nanqiao;

sentences.zh: 尚書婦是江夏王女，檀珪祖姑嬪長沙景王；

translations.literal: The Minister's wife was daughter of the Prince of Jiangxia; Tan Gui's great-aunt was consort to Prince Jing of Changsha;
translations.idiomatic: your wife is a daughter of the Prince of Jiangxia; my great-aunt was consort to Prince Jing of Changsha;

sentences.zh: 尚書伯爲江州，檀珪祖亦爲江州；

translations.literal: The Minister's uncle was Jiangzhou; Tan Gui's grandfather was also Jiangzhou;
translations.idiomatic: your uncle served as inspector of Jiangzhou, and my grandfather held the same post;

sentences.zh: 尚書從兄出身爲後軍參軍，檀珪父釋褐亦爲中軍參軍。

translations.literal: The Minister's cousin by birth first entered as rear-army staff officer; Tan Gui's father on leaving office robes also became central-army staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: your cousin first took office as staff officer on the rear-army command; when my father left the academy he too became staff officer on the central-army command.

sentences.zh: 僕於尚書，人地本懸，至於婚宦，不肯殊絕。

translations.literal: I toward the Minister in person and ground were always far apart; as to marriage and office, I would not be utterly set apart.
translations.idiomatic: Between us, I know, birth and standing were always far apart — yet in marriage and rank I should not have been cut off altogether.

sentences.zh: 今通塞雖異，猶忝氣類，尚書何事乃爾見苦？

translations.literal: Now though passage and blockage differ, still I share the breath-class — Minister, why must you torment me so?
translations.idiomatic: Today our fortunes differ, but we are still of the same kin. Minister, why must you treat me with such bitterness?

sentences.zh: 泰始之初，八表同逆，一門二世，粉骨衞主，殊勳異績，已不能甄，常階舊途，復見侵抑。

translations.literal: At the opening of Taishi, the eight directions rebelled together; one house two generations ground bone guarding the lord — extraordinary merit and service could not be distinguished; on the regular steps of the old path I again see suppression.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Taishi era the empire revolted on every side; two generations of my house shattered their bones in the sovereign's defense — yet such service could not win its due reward, and on the old ladder of promotion I am pushed down again.

sentences.zh: 」僧虔報書曰：「征北板比歲處遇小優，殷主簿從此府入崇禮，何儀曹卽代殷，亦不見訴爲苦。

translations.literal: 」Sengqian replied in a letter: 「These years the Pacify-North staff has been slightly better in treatment; Registrar Yin went from this office into Chongli; Master of Ceremony He at once replaced Yin — also no complaint that it was bitter.
translations.idiomatic: 」Sengqian wrote back: 「In recent years the Pacify-the-North staff has been treated somewhat more generously. Registrar Yin left this office for Chongli, and Master of Ceremony He replaced him at once — yet Yin never complained that he had suffered.

sentences.zh: 足下積屈，一朝超升，政自小難。

translations.literal: Your accumulated grievances, one morning leaping upward — truly a little hard.
translations.idiomatic: You have been wronged for years; to rise in a single morning is bound to feel hard.

sentences.zh: 泰始初勤苦十年，自未見其賞，而頓就求稱，亦何可遂。

translations.literal: From the opening of Taishi, ten years of bitter toil — I have not seen its reward; yet suddenly you press for rank — how can that be granted?
translations.idiomatic: From the beginning of Taishi you toiled bitterly for ten years without seeing reward; to demand a title all at once — how can that be allowed?

sentences.zh: 吾與足下素無怨憾，何以相侵苦，直是意有佐佑耳。

translations.literal: You and I from of old have no resentment — why mutual torment? It is simply that intent has favorites.
translations.idiomatic: You and I have never borne each other ill will — why this mutual harassment? It is only that favor follows preference.

sentences.zh: 」珪又書曰：「昔荀公達漢之功臣，晉武帝方爵其玄孫。

translations.literal: 」Gui wrote again: 「Of old Xun Gongda was a Han merit minister — Jin Wudi only then ennobled his great-grandson.
translations.idiomatic: 」Gui wrote again: 「Long ago Xun Yu was a pillar of the Han; only under Emperor Wu of Jin was his great-grandson ennobled.

sentences.zh: 夏侯惇魏氏勳佐，金德初融，亦始就甄顯，方賞其孫，封樹近族。

translations.literal: Xiahou Dun was a Wei merit aide — when the golden virtue first united, also only then were honors begun and shown; only then his grandson was rewarded and near kin enfeoffed and planted.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Dun was a founding aide of Wei; when the Jin first took the throne, his house was only then singled out for honor, his grandson rewarded and near kin enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 羊叔子以晉泰始中建策伐吳，至咸寧末，方加褒寵，封其兄子。

translations.literal: Uncle Yangzi at Jin Taishi raised the plan to attack Wu — only by the end of Xiankeng were favor and reward heaped, enfeoffing his brother's son.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu at the opening of Jin proposed the campaign against Wu; only at the end of the Xiankeng era was his merit rewarded, when his brother's son was enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 卞望之以咸和初殞身國難，至興寧末，方崇禮秩，官其子孫。

translations.literal: Bian Wangzhi at the opening of Xiankang died body for the state's calamity — only by the end of Xingning were rites and ranks honored, making posts for his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Hu perished for the state at the start of the Xiankang era; only at the end of Xingning were rites and rank restored to his descendants.

sentences.zh: 蜀郡主簿田混，黃初末死故君之難，咸康中方擢其子孫。

translations.literal: Shu commandery registrar Tian Hun — at the end of Huangchu died for the former lord's calamity; in the middle of Xiankang only then were his descendants promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Hun, registrar of Shu commandery, died for his fallen lord at the end of the Huangchu era; only midway through Xiankang were his descendants raised to office.

sentences.zh: 似不以世代遠而被棄，年世疏而見遺。

translations.literal: As if not because generations are remote to be cast away, because years are distant to be overlooked.
translations.idiomatic: Merit, it seems, is not cast aside because generations are distant, nor forgotten because years have passed.

sentences.zh: 檀珪百罹六極，造化罕比，五喪停露，百口轉命，存亡披迫，本希小祿，無意階榮。

translations.literal: Tan Gui hundred hardships six extremities, creation rarely matched; five funerals suspended in dew, hundred mouths shifting fate, existence and death pressed urgent — originally hoped small salary, no intent to climb glory.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Gui has known every extremity of fortune; heaven and earth offer few parallels. Five dead lie unburied, a hundred mouths hang on his breath; pressed between life and death, he asked only a modest stipend and never sought glory.

sentences.zh: 自古以來有沐食侯，近代有王官。

translations.literal: Since antiquity there have been bath-grant-eating marquises; in recent times there have been palace attendant posts.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity there have been marquises who lived on bath-grant income; in recent times there are palace attendants who draw stipends from court.

sentences.zh: 府佐非沐食之職，參軍非王官之謂。

translations.literal: Staff aide is not bath-grant-eating office; staff officer is not palace-attendant designation.
translations.idiomatic: A staff aide is no salaried fief post, and a staff officer is no court sinecure.

sentences.zh: 質非匏瓜，實羞空懸。

translations.literal: Substance is not gourd melon; truly ashamed at hanging empty.
translations.idiomatic: I am no ornamental gourd hung out to dry — yet that is exactly the shame I live in.

sentences.zh: 殷、何二生，或是府主情味，或是朝廷意旨，豈與悠悠之人同口而語。

translations.literal: Yin and He, the two men — perhaps the lord's taste, perhaps the court's intent — how can one speak in the same mouth as drifting common folk?
translations.idiomatic: Yin and He may answer to the prince's fancy or the court's will — how can they be named in the same breath as men like me?

sentences.zh: 使僕就此職，尚書能以郎見轉不？

translations.literal: If you make me take this office — can the Minister transfer me with a gentleman-of-the-palace view?
translations.idiomatic: If you force me into this post, will you not at least advance me to a palace gentleman's rank?

sentences.zh: 若使日得五升祿，則不恥執鞭。

translations.literal: If I might daily receive five sheng salary, I would not be ashamed to hold the whip.
translations.idiomatic: Give me five sheng of grain a day and I would not be ashamed to tend horses at your gate.

sentences.zh: 」僧虔乃用爲安城郡丞。

translations.literal: 」Sengqian thereupon employed him as Ancheng commandery assistant.
translations.idiomatic: 」Sengqian then appointed him assistant magistrate of Ancheng commandery.

sentences.zh: 珪，宋安南將軍韶孫也。

translations.literal: Gui was grandson of Song Pacify-South General Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was grandson of Shao, Pacify-South general of Song.

sentences.zh: 僧虔尋加散騎常侍，轉右僕射。

translations.literal: Sengqian soon added irregular cavalry attendant, shifted to right vice director.
translations.idiomatic: Sengqian was soon made irregular attendant of the cavalry and then right vice director.

sentences.zh: 昇明元年，遷尚書僕射，尋轉中書令，左僕射，二年，爲尚書令。

translations.literal: Shengming year 1, shifted to vice director of the ministry of state; soon shifted to directorate of the palace, left vice director; year 2, made director of the ministry of state.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shengming he was made vice director of the ministry of state, then directorate of the palace and left vice director; in the second year he became director of the ministry of state.

sentences.zh: 僧虔好文史，解音律，以朝廷禮樂多違正典，民閒競造新聲雜曲，時太祖輔政，僧虔上表曰：「夫懸鍾之器，以雅爲用；

translations.literal: Sengqian loved literature and history, understood music theory — because court ritual music often violated the orthodox canon, the folk competing to make new sounds and mixed tunes, the Grand Ancestor aiding government; Sengqian memorialized: 「Hanging-bell vessels — with elegance as their use;
translations.idiomatic: Sengqian loved letters and history and understood music. Because court ritual and music often strayed from the canon while the people rushed to invent new airs, and with the founding emperor then assisting government, Sengqian submitted a memorial: 「Suspended bells are instruments of the elegant style;

sentences.zh: 凱容之禮，八佾爲儀。

translations.literal: Triumphal-appearance rites — eight files of dancers as ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: the Rites of Triumphant Bearing take the eight ranks of dancers as their measure.

sentences.zh: 今總章羽佾，音服舛異。

translations.literal: Now the Zongzhang feather dancers — music and dress at odds.
translations.idiomatic: Today the dancers of Zongzhang in feathered costume differ in both music and dress.

sentences.zh: 又歌鍾一肆，克諧女樂，以歌爲務，非雅器也。

translations.literal: Also song-bells one set, able to harmonize with female music, making song the task — not elegant vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Also, a full set of chiming bells has been tuned to female entertainers and made to serve song — no instrument of the elegant style.

sentences.zh: 大明中，卽以宮懸合和《鞞》、《拂》，節數雖會，慮乖《雅》體，將來知音，或譏聖世。

translations.literal: In Daming, at once used palace-suspended bells to harmonize the 「Shield」 and 「Scepter」 — though beat counts match, I fear straying from the Ya form; future connoisseurs of music may ridicule our sage age.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daming era the court suspended bells were set to accompany the Shield and Flywhisk dances; though the beats align, I fear the spirit of the Ya music is lost, and later masters of tone may laugh at our age.

sentences.zh: 若謂鍾舞已諧，重違成憲，更立歌鍾，不參舊例。

translations.literal: If it is said bell-dance is already harmonious, again to violate standing statutes — establish separate song-bells, not joining old precedent.
translations.idiomatic: If the court holds that bells and dance are already harmonized and will not break established statutes, then set up separate song-bells and keep them outside the old pattern.

sentences.zh: 四縣所奏，謹依《雅》條，卽義沿理。

translations.literal: What the four counties perform — strictly following Ya provisions — then meaning along reason.
translations.idiomatic: Let what the four districts perform follow the rules of the Ya music in strict accord — that accords with both ritual and reason.

sentences.zh: 如或可附。

translations.literal: If perhaps it can be appended.
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps this may be adopted.

sentences.zh: 又今之清商，實由銅爵，三祖風流，遺音盈耳，京、洛相高，江左彌貴。

translations.literal: Also today's Pure Shang — in fact from the Bronze Pavilion; the three ancestors' elegant style, surviving tones fill the ear; Jing and Luo esteem it, Jiang left treasures it more.
translations.idiomatic: As for today's Pure Shang melodies, they descend from the Bronze Bird Terrace; the elegant music of the three founders still rings in men's ears, prized in the northern capitals and treasured all the more in the south.

sentences.zh: 諒以金石干羽，事絕私室，桑、濮、鄭、衞，訓隔紳冕，中庸和雅，莫復於斯。

translations.literal: Surely stone and metal and dried feathers — affairs end in private chambers; Mulberry, Pu, Zheng, Wei — instruction separates from court caps and robes; mean harmony and elegance — none recovers here.
translations.idiomatic: Stone bells and feathered pipes belong not to private halls; the music of Mulberry, Pu, Zheng, and Wei was barred from court by the sages; nowhere should refined harmony be restored more than here.

sentences.zh: 而情變聽移，稍復銷落，十數年閒，亡者將半。

translations.literal: Yet feelings change and hearing shifts — gradually again fades and falls; within ten-odd years, those lost will be half.
translations.idiomatic: Yet as taste changes and hearing shifts, it fades away; within a dozen years nearly half will be gone.

sentences.zh: 自頃家競新哇，人尚謠俗，務在噍殺，不顧音紀，流宕無崖，未知所極，排斥正曲，崇長煩淫。

translations.literal: Recently households compete in new tunes, people esteem folk songs; intent on shrill killing tones, not caring for music rules, drifting without shore, unknown limit, excluding correct melodies, exalting lengthy licentiousness.
translations.idiomatic: Lately every household vies in vulgar novelty and every man chases street ballads, caring only for shrill and fractured tones and not for musical law. The fashion drifts without limit, repels the canonical airs, and exalts what is elaborate and licentious.

sentences.zh: 士有等差，無故不可去樂；

translations.literal: Scholars have grades of rank; without cause they may not cast off music;
translations.idiomatic: Men of rank stand in their grades; without good cause they must not abandon music;

sentences.zh: 禮有攸序，長幼不可共聞。

translations.literal: rites have their proper order; elder and younger may not hear the same pieces.
translations.idiomatic: ritual has its sequence; what the elder hears must not be shared with the younger.

sentences.zh: 故喧醜之制，日盛於里；

translations.literal: Thus rowdy and ugly pieces daily flourish in the lanes;
translations.idiomatic: So the vulgar and clamorous pieces grow louder in the lanes day by day;

sentences.zh: 風味之響，獨盡於衣冠。

translations.literal: while refined strains are exhausted only among those in cap and gown.
translations.idiomatic: while what is fine in flavor lingers only among the gentry in cap and gown.

sentences.zh: 宜命有司，務懃功課，緝理遺逸，迭相開曉，所經漏忘，悉加補綴。

translations.literal: It is fitting to charge the responsible offices to press hard on their duties, gather and set in order what was lost or scattered, take turns in instructing and clarifying, and wherever omissions and lapses occurred, repair them entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Let the responsible offices be charged to drive their work hard, gather what was lost, teach one another in turn, and wherever something was missed or forgotten, stitch it back into place.

sentences.zh: 曲全者祿厚，藝妙者位優。

translations.literal: Those who preserve a piece entire should receive thick stipends; those whose art is subtle should rank higher.
translations.idiomatic: Full mastery of a piece should win a fat stipend; subtle mastery should win the better seat.

sentences.zh: 利以動之，則人思刻厲。

translations.literal: Move them with gain, and men will think to carve themselves sharp.
translations.idiomatic: Stir them with profit, and men will drive themselves to hone their craft.

sentences.zh: 反本還源，庶可跂踵。

translations.literal: Return to the root and turn back to the source, and perhaps they may tread on one another's heels again.
translations.idiomatic: Turn back to root and source, and perhaps they may catch the old pace again.

sentences.zh: 」事見納。

translations.literal: 」The matter was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was adopted.

sentences.zh: 建元元年，轉侍中，撫軍將軍，丹陽尹。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan he was transferred to regular attendant, Pacification Army general, and intendant of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jianyuan's first year saw him made regular attendant, Pacification Army general, and intendant of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 二年，進號左衞將軍，固讓不拜。

translations.literal: In the second year he was promoted in title to Left Guard General but firmly declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The second year brought promotion to Left Guard General; he declined firmly and would not take it.

sentences.zh: 改授左光祿大夫，侍中、尹如故。

translations.literal: He was reassigned Left Grand Master of the Splendid Hall; regular attendant and intendant stood as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was given instead the Left Grand Master of the Splendid Hall, while keeping regular attendant and the intendantcy.

sentences.zh: 郡縣獄相承有上湯殺囚，僧虔上疏言之曰：「湯本以救疾，而實行冤暴，或以肆忿。

translations.literal: In district and county prisons the custom continued of reporting upward with hot water to kill prisoners; Sengqian memorialized, saying: 「Hot water was originally meant to heal the sick, but in practice it brought wrongful violence—or served merely to vent rage.
translations.idiomatic: District and county jails still carried on the custom of reporting hot-water baths to kill prisoners; Sengqian memorialized: 「Hot water was meant to heal the sick, yet in practice it worked injustice—or vented private rage.

sentences.zh: 若罪必入重，自有正刑；

translations.literal: If the crime truly fell within the heavy punishments, proper penalty existed of its own;
translations.idiomatic: If guilt truly warranted the heavy code, the proper punishments were already there;

sentences.zh: 若去惡宜疾，則應先啟。

translations.literal: if evil must be removed swiftly, report should come first.
translations.idiomatic: if evil had to be cut down fast, word should go up first.

sentences.zh: 豈有死生大命，而潛制下邑。

translations.literal: How could the great mandate of life and death be secretly controlled in the lower counties?
translations.idiomatic: How could the supreme charge of life and death be wielded in secret by a distant county?

sentences.zh: 愚謂治下囚病，必先刺郡，求職司與醫對共診驗；

translations.literal: I hold that when a prisoner below falls ill, one must first memorialize the prefecture and request that the duty officer and physician examine and verify together;
translations.idiomatic: My foolish view is that a sick prisoner must first be reported to the prefecture, and the duty officer made to face a physician in joint diagnosis;

sentences.zh: 遠縣，家人省視，然後處理。

translations.literal: in distant counties, let the family visit and view him, then dispose of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: in remote counties, let kin see him first, and only then act.

sentences.zh: 可使死者不恨，生者無怨。

translations.literal: Thus the dead would bear no resentment and the living no complaint.
translations.idiomatic: Then the dead would die without hate and the living live without grievance.

sentences.zh: 」上納其言。

translations.literal: 」The emperor accepted his words.
translations.idiomatic: 」The throne took his counsel.

sentences.zh: 僧虔留意雅樂，昇明中所奏，雖微有釐改，尚多遺失。

translations.literal: Sengqian gave his heart to elegant music; what was performed in the Shengming era, though slightly corrected here and there, still had many omissions.
translations.idiomatic: Sengqian cared deeply for the elegant repertoire; the pieces set forth in Shengming, though tweaked in spots, were still riddled with losses.

sentences.zh: 是時上始欲通使，僧虔與兄子儉書曰：「古語云『中國失禮，問之四夷』。

translations.literal: At that time the sovereign was first intending to send envoys abroad; Sengqian wrote to his nephew Jian: 「The old saying runs, 『When the Central States lose ritual, one inquires of the four barbarians.』
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign was first thinking of sending envoys; Sengqian wrote his nephew Jian: 「There is an old saying: 『When the Middle Kingdom loses ritual, ask the four quarters.』

sentences.zh: 計樂亦如。

translations.literal: I reckon music is the same.
translations.idiomatic: I reckon music is no different.

sentences.zh: 苻堅敗後，東晉始備金石樂，故知不可全誣也。

translations.literal: After Fu Jian's defeat, Eastern Jin first completed metal-and-stone music—so one knows it cannot all be dismissed as deceit.
translations.idiomatic: After Fu Jian fell, Eastern Jin at last had metal and stone again—proof that not everything can be written off as pretense.

sentences.zh: 北國或有遺樂，誠未可便以補中夏之闕，且得知其存亡，亦一理也。

translations.literal: The northern realm may hold surviving pieces, but truly one cannot lightly use them to plug gaps in central China; yet simply to learn whether they still live or perish is also a kind of reason.
translations.idiomatic: The north may still have stray pieces, yet one must not rashly pad the Central Lands' breaches with them; still, to learn whether they survive is reason enough.

sentences.zh: 但《鼓吹》舊有二十一曲，今所能者十一而已，意謂北使會有散役，得今樂署一人粗別同異者，充此使限。

translations.literal: But the old Drumming and Blowing had twenty-one pieces, and only eleven can be played today—I think that when northern envoys come there may be scattered attendants; let the Music Office supply one man who can roughly sort sameness from difference, and attach him to this embassy's quota.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the old Drumming and Blowing held twenty-one pieces, and only eleven remain playable—I think the northern embassy may bring stray servants; let the Music Office lend one man who can roughly tell like from unlike, and count him toward the mission's roster.

sentences.zh: 雖復延州難追，其得知所知，亦當不同。

translations.literal: Though Yanzhou's music is hard to recover, what is known when known would also differ.
translations.idiomatic: Even if Yanzhou's tunes cannot be chased down, what knowledge meets knowledge would still not be the same.

sentences.zh: 若謂有此理者，可得申吾意上聞否？

translations.literal: If you find sense in this reasoning, could you bring my intent upward for me?
translations.idiomatic: If you think the reasoning holds, might you carry my meaning to the throne?

sentences.zh: 試爲思之。

translations.literal: Try to think it through.
translations.idiomatic: Think it through and tell me.

sentences.zh: 」事竟不行。

translations.literal: 」In the end it was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: 」Nothing came of it.

sentences.zh: 太祖善書，及卽位，篤好不已。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor was skilled at calligraphy, and after taking the throne his deep love did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor wrote well, and once he held the throne his passion only deepened.

sentences.zh: 與僧虔賭書畢，謂僧虔曰：「誰爲第一？

translations.literal: Having finished a calligraphy wager with Sengqian, he said to Sengqian: 「Who ranks first?
translations.idiomatic: When a calligraphy match with Sengqian was done, he asked him: 「Who is first?

sentences.zh: 」僧虔曰：「臣書第一，陛下亦第一。

translations.literal: 」Sengqian said: 「My calligraphy is first, and Your Majesty's is also first.
translations.idiomatic: 」Sengqian said: 「Mine ranks first, and Your Majesty's ranks first as well.

sentences.zh: 」上笑曰：「卿可謂善自爲謀矣。

translations.literal: 」The emperor laughed: 「You may be said to know how to look out for yourself.
translations.idiomatic: 」The emperor laughed: 「You know how to scheme on your own behalf.

sentences.zh: 」示僧虔古迹十一袠，就求能書人名。

translations.literal: 」He showed Sengqian eleven bundles of ancient works and asked at once for the names of able calligraphers.
translations.idiomatic: 」He showed Sengqian eleven fascicles of ancient work and bade him list who wrote well.

sentences.zh: 僧虔得民閒所有，袠中所無者，吳大皇帝、景帝、歸命侯書，桓玄書，及王丞相導、領軍洽、中書令珉、張芝、索靖、衞伯儒、張翼十二卷奏之。

translations.literal: Sengqian obtained what was in common circulation but absent from the bundles—the Great Emperor of Wu, Emperor Jing, the script of the Marquis of Guiming, Huan Xuan's script, and Chancellor of State Dao, Pacification Army Qia, Secretariat Director Min, Zhang Zhi, Suo Jing, Wei Boyu, Zhang Yi—twelve fascicles in all, and memorialized them.
translations.idiomatic: What Sengqian found in the world but not in the bundles were pieces by Wu's Great Emperor, Emperor Jing, the Marquis of Guiming, Huan Xuan, Chancellor Wang Dao, Pacification Army Wang Qia, Secretariat Director Wang Min, Zhang Zhi, Suo Jing, Wei Boyu, and Zhang Yi—twelve fascicles in all, which he submitted.

sentences.zh: 又上羊欣所撰《能書人名》一卷。

translations.literal: He also submitted one fascicle of Yang Xin's Names of Able Calligraphers.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted Yang Xin's one-fascicle Names of Able Calligraphers.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，遷持節、都督湘州諸軍事、征南將軍、湘州刺史，侍中如故。

translations.literal: That winter he was moved to Bearer of the Staff over military affairs in Xiang Province, Southern Expedition general, and inspector of Xiangzhou; regular attendant stood as before.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he went out as Bearer of the Staff over Xiang Province, Southern Expedition general, and inspector of Xiangzhou, while keeping regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 清簡無所欲，不營財產，百姓安之。

translations.literal: Pure and spare, he desired nothing, did not pursue wealth, and the hundred clans lived in peace under him.
translations.idiomatic: He was spare and clear of want, built no fortune, and the people beneath him rested easy.

sentences.zh: 世祖卽位，僧虔以風疾欲陳解，會遷侍中、左光祿大夫、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: When Shizu took the throne, Sengqian, owing to wind ailment, wished to memorialize his resignation; chanced instead to be moved to regular attendant, Left Grand Master of the Splendid Hall, and Merit Equal to the Founding Duke.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu acceded, Sengqian—afflicted with wind numbness—meant to resign by memorial, but was instead raised to regular attendant, Left Grand Master of the Splendid Hall, and Merit Equal to the Founding Duke.

sentences.zh: 僧虔少時羣從宗族竝會，客有相之者云：「僧虔年位最高，仕當至公，餘人莫及也。

translations.literal: When Sengqian was young the cousins of the clan all gathered; a visitor who read fortunes said: 「Of you all Sengqian's years and rank will stand highest; in office he should reach the chief ministers—none of the rest can match him.
translations.idiomatic: In youth the clan cousins all met; a fortune-teller among the guests said: 「Sengqian will outlive and outrank you all—he is fated for the highest office, and none of the rest will touch him.

sentences.zh: 」及授，僧虔謂兄子儉曰：「汝任重於朝，行當有八命之禮，我若復此授，則一門有二台司，實可畏懼。

translations.literal: 」When the appointment arrived, Sengqian told his nephew Jian: 「You bear heavy weight at court and will soon receive the eightfold rites of office; if I took this appointment again, one household would hold two terrace ministers—a thing to fear indeed.
translations.idiomatic: 」When the appointment came, Sengqian told his nephew Jian: 「You already carry the court's weight and will soon take the eightfold rites; if I took this post too, one house would seat two terrace ministers—that is a thing to dread.

sentences.zh: 」乃固辭不拜，上優而許之。

translations.literal: 」He therefore declined firmly and would not accept; the emperor favored him and granted permission.
translations.idiomatic: 」He refused firmly and would not bow to it; the throne was gracious and let him go.

sentences.zh: 改授侍中、特進、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was reassigned regular attendant, special advancement, and Left Grand Master of the Splendid Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was given instead regular attendant, special advancement, and Left Grand Master of the Splendid Hall.

sentences.zh: 客問僧虔固讓之意，僧虔曰：「君子所憂無德，不憂無寵。

translations.literal: A visitor asked the intent behind his firm declination; Sengqian said: 「What the gentleman worries over is lack of virtue, not lack of favor.
translations.idiomatic: A guest asked why he had refused so hard; Sengqian said: 「A gentleman fears lacking virtue, not lacking favor.

sentences.zh: 吾衣食周身，榮位已過，所慚庸薄無以報國，豈容更受高爵，方貽官謗邪！

translations.literal: My clothing and food already cover my person; glory and rank have passed their measure—what shames me is dull mediocrity with no way to repay the state. How could I still take exalted titles and court official censure!
translations.idiomatic: I am already clothed and fed; honor has outrun my worth. What shames me is mediocrity that cannot repay the realm—how then take a higher rank and invite the censor's lash?

sentences.zh: 」兄子儉爲朝宰，起長梁齋，制度小過，僧虔視之不悅，竟不入戶，儉卽毀之。

translations.literal: Nephew Jian was chief minister; he raised a Hall of the Long Beam whose regulations overshot the mark slightly; Sengqian looked on it displeased and in the end would not cross the threshold—whereupon Jian at once had it torn down.
translations.idiomatic: Nephew Jian was chief minister and built a Hall of the Long Beam whose scale edged past propriety; Sengqian looked on it with displeasure and never crossed the door—so Jian tore it down at once.

sentences.zh: 永明三年，薨。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongming he died.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming's third year he died.

sentences.zh: 僧虔頗解星文，夜坐見豫章分野當有事故，時僧虔子慈爲豫章內史，慮其有公事。

translations.literal: Sengqian was quite versed in star lore; sitting at night he saw that the astral field of Yuzhang should soon meet trouble; at the time his son Ci was interior administrator of Yuzhang, and he feared official business there.
translations.idiomatic: Sengqian knew the stars well; one night he saw trouble brewing in Yuzhang's allotment—his son Ci was then interior administrator there, and he feared some public crisis.

sentences.zh: 少時，僧虔薨，慈棄郡奔赴。

translations.literal: Before long Sengqian died; Ci abandoned the commandery and raced to mourn.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Sengqian died; Ci left his post and rushed home on the funeral road.

sentences.zh: 僧虔時年六十。

translations.literal: Sengqian was then sixty years old.
translations.idiomatic: Sengqian was sixty at the time.

sentences.zh: 追贈司空，侍中如故。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given Minister of Works; palace attendant unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: After death he was made minister of works, with palace attendant unchanged.

sentences.zh: 諡簡穆。

translations.literal: Posthumous title: Refined and Solemn.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Jianmu, Refined and Solemn.

sentences.zh: 其論書曰：「宋文帝書，自云可比王子敬，時議者云『天然勝羊欣，功夫少於欣』。

translations.literal: His treatise on calligraphy says: 「Emperor Wen of Song's writing—he himself said it could match Wang Zijing; critics of the day said, 「His natural gift surpasses Yang Xin's, but trained skill falls short of Xin's.」
translations.idiomatic: In his discourse on calligraphy he wrote: 「Emperor Wen of Song claimed his hand could stand beside Wang Zijing's; men of the time said, 「By native gift he outdoes Yang Xin, yet in practiced craft he trails Xin.」

sentences.zh: 王平南廙、右軍叔，過江之前以爲最。

translations.literal: Wang Pingnan Yi, the Right General's uncle, were held the finest before the crossing south.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pingnan Yi, uncle to the Right General, were reckoned the best before the river crossing.

sentences.zh: 亡曾祖領軍書，右軍云『弟書遂不減吾』。

translations.literal: My deceased great-grandfather the commandant-in-chief's writing—the Right General said, 「Younger brother's script does not fall short of mine.」
translations.idiomatic: Of my late great-grandfather the commandant-in-chief's hand, the Right General said, 「The younger brother's writing in no way diminishes mine.」

sentences.zh: 變古制，今唯右軍。

translations.literal: He changed the ancient manner; today only the Right General does so.
translations.idiomatic: He broke with the old forms; today only the Right General has done the same.

sentences.zh: 領軍不爾，至今猶法鍾、張。

translations.literal: The commandant-in-chief did not; to this day he still takes Zhong and Zhang as his model.
translations.idiomatic: The commandant-in-chief did not; even now his line still follows Zhong and Zhang.

sentences.zh: 亡從祖中書令書，子敬云『弟書如騎騾，駸駸恒欲度驊騮前』。

translations.literal: My deceased collateral ancestor the director of the Secretariat's writing—Zijing said, 「Younger brother's script is like riding a mule, always straining to pass the bay ahead.」
translations.idiomatic: My late collateral forebear the director of the Secretariat—Zijing said of his hand, 「The younger brother writes as one rides a mule, forever lunging to get past the thoroughbred in front.」

sentences.zh: 庾征西翼書，少時與右軍齊名，右軍後進，庾猶不分，在荊州與都下人書云：『小兒輩賤家雞，皆學逸少書，須吾下，當比之。

translations.literal: Western Campaigning General Yu Yi's writing—in youth he ranked with the Right General; the Right General later pulled ahead, yet Yu still would not concede. Writing from Jingzhou to someone at court he said: 「Those wretched village chickens of the younger set all study Yi Shao's script. It will take me to come down before they can be matched.
translations.idiomatic: Western campaigning general Yu Yi—in his youth he stood even with the Right General; the Right General later outpaced him, yet Yu would still not yield. From Jingzhou he wrote someone in the capital: 「Every wretched barnyard fowl among the young imitates Yi Shao's hand. Wait until I come down—then they may be compared.

sentences.zh: 』張翼，王右軍自書表，晉穆帝令翼寫題後答，右軍當時不別，久後方悟，云『小人幾欲亂真』。

translations.literal: 」Zhang Yi: when the Right General Wang personally wrote a memorial, Emperor Mu of Jin had Yi copy it and write the heading for the reply; at the time the Right General could not tell them apart; only long afterward did he realize and say, 「The fellow nearly passed for the genuine article.」
translations.idiomatic: 」Zhang Yi: when the Right General Wang drafted a memorial himself, Emperor Mu of Jin had Yi copy it and pen the heading on the reply; at the time the Right General could not tell which was which; only much later did he see through it and say, 「The little man nearly turned truth upside down.」

sentences.zh: 張芝、索靖、韋誕、鍾會、二衞竝得名前代，無以辨其優劣，唯見其筆力驚異耳。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhi, Suo Jing, Wei Dan, Zhong Hui, and the two Weis all won fame in earlier ages—there is no distinguishing their relative merit; one only sees their brush strength was startling and extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhi, Suo Jing, Wei Dan, Zhong Hui, and the two Weis all made names in former times; one cannot sort their ranks—only that their brushwork struck the eye as uncanny.

sentences.zh: 張澄當時亦呼有意。

translations.literal: Zhang Cheng at the time was also said to have intent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cheng in his day was likewise called a man of purpose.

sentences.zh: 郗愔章草亞於右軍。

translations.literal: Xi Kai's draft-clerical script ranked below the Right General.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Kai's draft clerical stood beneath the Right General's.

sentences.zh: 郗嘉賔草亞於二王，緊媚過其父。

translations.literal: Xi Jiabin's cursive ranked below the Two Wangs, but was tighter and more delicate than his father's.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jiabin's cursive trailed the Two Wangs, yet was more compact and graceful than his father's.

sentences.zh: 桓玄自謂右軍之流，論者以比孔琳之。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan styled himself of the Right General's school; critics compared him to Kong Linzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan called himself of the Right General's line; reviewers set him beside Kong Linzhi.

sentences.zh: 謝安亦入能書錄，亦自重，爲子敬書嵇康詩。

translations.literal: Xie An also entered the register of able calligraphers; he too thought highly of himself and wrote Xi Kang's poetry for Zijing.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An too made the roll of able calligraphers, prized his own hand, and wrote out Xi Kang's poems for Zijing.

sentences.zh: 羊欣書見重一時，親受子敬，行書尤善，正乃不稱名。

translations.literal: Yang Xin's writing was esteemed for a time; he received instruction personally from Zijing; running script he excelled at especially; regular script simply did not earn him a name.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xin's hand was honored for a season; he studied face to face with Zijing; in running script he shone, yet in regular script he never won a name.

sentences.zh: 孔琳之書天然放縱，極有筆力，規矩恐在羊欣後。

translations.literal: Kong Linzhi's writing was naturally free and unrestrained, with extreme brush strength; in formal rules he probably fell behind Yang Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Linzhi wrote with native abandon and fearsome stroke; in measure and rule he likely stood behind Yang Xin.

sentences.zh: 丘道護與羊欣俱面受子敬，故當在欣後。

translations.literal: Qiu Daohu and Yang Xin both received Zijing face to face, so he should rank after Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Daohu and Yang Xin both sat before Zijing in person; Daohu therefore belongs after Xin.

sentences.zh: 范曅與蕭思話同師羊欣，後小叛，旣失故步，爲復小有意耳。

translations.literal: Fan Ye and Xiao Sihua studied under Yang Xin together; later Ye turned rebel a little; having lost his former footing, only retained a little intent.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ye and Xiao Sihua shared Yang Xin as teacher; later Ye slipped a little from the path, lost his old step, and kept only a trace of purpose.

sentences.zh: 蕭思話書，羊欣之影，風流趣好，殆當不減，筆力恨弱。

translations.literal: Xiao Sihua's writing is Yang Xin's shadow—in elegant taste nearly not inferior, but brush strength regrettably weak.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Sihua's hand is Yang Xin's shadow: in ease and taste he nearly does not fall short, yet his stroke power is painfully thin.

sentences.zh: 謝綜書，其舅云『緊生起，是得賞也，恨少媚好』。

translations.literal: Xie Zong's writing—his uncle said, 「Tightness arises in him—that earns praise—but regrettably little charm.」
translations.idiomatic: On Xie Zong's writing his uncle said, 「He is tightening up—that wins praise—but alas, too little sweetness.」

sentences.zh: 謝靈運乃不倫，遇其合時，亦得入流。

translations.literal: Xie Lingyun was simply out of category; when he hit his moment, he too could enter the current.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Lingyun was simply not of the same breed; when the fit was right, he too could join the stream.

sentences.zh: 賀道力書亞丘道護。

translations.literal: He Daoli's writing ranked below Qiu Daohu.
translations.idiomatic: He Daoli's hand stood beneath Qiu Daohu's.

sentences.zh: 庾昕學右軍，亦欲亂真矣。

translations.literal: Yu Xin studied the Right General and also nearly passed for genuine.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xin trained on the Right General and likewise came close to passing for the real thing.

sentences.zh: 」又著《書賦》，傳於世。

translations.literal: 」He also authored Rhapsody on Calligraphy, transmitted in the world.
translations.idiomatic: 」He also wrote Rhapsody on Calligraphy, which circulated in his time.

sentences.zh: 第九子寂，字子玄，性迅動，好文章，讀《范滂傳》，未常不歎挹。

translations.literal: His ninth son Ji, styled Zixuan, was quick and restless by nature, loved literature; reading the biography of Fan Peng, he never failed to sigh in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: His ninth son Ji, styled Zixuan, was swift and restless by nature and loved letters; whenever he read the biography of Fan Peng he could not keep from sighing in wonder.

sentences.zh: 王融敗後，賔客多歸之。

translations.literal: After Wang Rong's defeat, many clients turned to him.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Rong's fall, many of his former guests attached themselves to Ji.

sentences.zh: 建武初，欲獻《中興頌》，兄志謂之曰：「汝膏粱年少，何患不達，不鎮之以靜，將恐貽譏。

translations.literal: Early in Jianwu, he wished to present Ode on Restoration; his elder brother Zhi told him: 「You are a young man of fattened grain—what need to worry you will not rise? If you do not steady yourself with quiet, you will probably invite ridicule.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Jianwu he meant to offer an Ode on Restoration; his elder brother Zhi told him, 「You are young, well-fed, and born to rank—what fear that you will not arrive? Without quiet to anchor you, you will only buy mockery.

sentences.zh: 」寂乃止。

translations.literal: 」Ji then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: 」Ji dropped the plan.

sentences.zh: 初爲祕書郎，卒，年二十一。

translations.literal: At first made Secretariat Gentleman; he died, aged twenty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He had first been made secretariat gentleman; he died at twenty-one.

sentences.zh: 僧虔宋世嘗有書誡子曰：

translations.literal: In Song times Sengqian once had a letter admonishing his son, which read:
translations.idiomatic: Under the Song, Sengqian once wrote his son a letter of warning that ran thus:

sentences.zh: 知汝恨吾不許汝學，欲自悔厲，或以闔棺自欺，或更擇美業，且得有慨，亦慰窮生。

translations.literal: I know you resent that I will not let you pursue learning, that you wish to discipline yourself—or deceive yourself with the coffin lid closed, or choose some finer pursuit anew; at least you have some indignation, which also consoles this poor life.
translations.idiomatic: I know you chafe that I forbid your studies, that you mean to whip yourself into shape—or fool yourself behind a closed coffin lid, or pick some brighter trade instead; still, that you feel something at all is a small comfort to this threadbare life.

sentences.zh: 但亟聞斯唱，未睹其實。

translations.literal: But I have often heard this tune, and never seen the reality.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I have heard this song too often and never once seen the deed.

sentences.zh: 請從先師聽言觀行，冀此不復虛身。

translations.literal: Please follow the former teachers—hear the words, watch the conduct—and hope this will not again hollow out your person.
translations.idiomatic: Take the old masters as your measure—listen to what they say, watch what they do—and perhaps you will not waste yourself again.

sentences.zh: 吾未信汝，非徒然也。

translations.literal: I do not yet trust you—and not without reason.
translations.idiomatic: I do not yet believe you, and not for nothing.

sentences.zh: 往年有意於史，取《三國志》聚置牀頭，百日許，復徙業就玄，自當小差於史，猶未近彷佛。

translations.literal: In past years you turned toward history, gathered the Records of the Three Kingdoms and piled them at the bedhead—for a hundred days or so—then shifted your pursuit to arcane learning; that should be a little inferior to history, yet you are still far from even an approximation.
translations.idiomatic: Years back you bent toward history, stacked the Records of the Three Kingdoms at your pillow, kept at it a hundred days or so, then changed course for the arcane arts—already a step down from history, and still nowhere near even a likeness.

sentences.zh: 曼倩有云：「談何容易。

translations.literal: Manqian said: 「How easily one talks!
translations.idiomatic: Manqian said, 「How lightly men talk!

sentences.zh: 」見諸玄，志爲之逸，腸爲之抽，專一書，轉誦數十家注，自少至老，手不釋卷，尚未敢輕言。

translations.literal: 」Seeing the arcane masters, his aspirations ran away with him, his guts twisted; fix on one book, turn through commentaries from several dozen schools—from youth to old age never releasing the scroll from hand—and still they dared not speak lightly.
translations.idiomatic: 」Before the masters of the arcane, the heart runs off and the bowels knot; they fix on a single text, cycle through glosses from dozens of houses—from boyhood to gray hair never letting the scroll leave the hand—and even then dare not speak rashly.

sentences.zh: 汝開《老子》卷頭五尺許，未知輔嗣何所道，平叔何所說，馬、鄭何所異，《指》《例》何所明，而便盛於麈尾，自呼談士，此最險事。

translations.literal: You open the Laozi scroll a foot or five through the head, do not know what Fu asserts, what Ping expounds, how Ma and Zheng differ, what the Pointers and Examples clarify—and at once flourish the fly-whisk and call yourself a disputation master: this is the most perilous course.
translations.idiomatic: You unfold the Laozi a foot or five into the first fascicle, yet cannot say what Fusi argued, what Pingshu taught, where Ma and Zheng part company, what the Pointers and Examples make plain—and already you brandish the fly-whisk and call yourself a talker. That is the deadliest folly.

sentences.zh: 設令袁令命汝言《易》，謝中書挑汝言《莊》，張吳興叩汝言《老》，端可復言未嘗看邪？

translations.literal: Suppose Master Yuan ordered you to expound the Changes, Secretariat Director Xie challenged you on Zhuangzi, Zhang of Wuxing pressed you on the Laozi—could you still say you had never looked?
translations.idiomatic: Suppose Magistrate Yuan bade you lecture on the Changes, Director Xie of the Secretariat goaded you on Zhuangzi, Zhang of Wuxing grilled you on the Laozi—would you still claim you had never opened them?

sentences.zh: 談故如射，前人得破，後人應解，不解卽輸賭矣。

translations.literal: Disputation is like archery: when the forehand scores a hit, the aft hand must answer; fail to answer and you lose the wager.
translations.idiomatic: Talk is like archery: when the first shooter finds the mark, the next must answer; fail to answer and you forfeit the match.

sentences.zh: 且論注百氏，荊州《八袠》，又《才性四本》，《聲無哀樂》，皆言家口實，如客至之有設也。

translations.literal: Besides, for commentaries on the hundred schools, the Jingzhou Eight Fascicles, also Four Roots of Talent and Nature and Sound Has No Grief or Joy—all are staples on the disputant's tongue, like dishes set out when guests arrive.
translations.idiomatic: And the commentaries of the hundred schools, the Jingzhou Eight Fascicles, the Four Roots of Talent and Nature, Sound Has No Grief or Joy—these are meat and drink on every debater's table, set out as soon as guests cross the threshold.

sentences.zh: 汝皆未經拂耳瞥目。

translations.literal: You have never passed them by your ear or your eye even in a glance.
translations.idiomatic: You have not brushed them past ear or eye even once.

sentences.zh: 豈有庖廚不脩，而欲延大賔者哉？

translations.literal: How can there be a kitchen untended yet you wish to entertain great guests?
translations.idiomatic: Who keeps an empty kitchen and still expects to feast great guests?

sentences.zh: 就如張衡思侔造化，郭象言類懸河，不自勞苦，何由至此？

translations.literal: Even Zhang Heng whose thought matched creation, Guo Xiang whose words seemed a hanging river—without wearing themselves out in labor, how could they reach that point?
translations.idiomatic: Even Zhang Heng, whose mind rivaled creation, and Guo Xiang, whose speech hung like a river in flood—without grinding themselves down, how could they have arrived there?

sentences.zh: 汝曾未窺其題目，未辨其指歸；

translations.literal: You have never even glimpsed their topics, never distinguished their aims;
translations.idiomatic: You have never so much as looked into their subjects or sorted out where they lead;

sentences.zh: 六十四卦，未知何名；

translations.literal: the sixty-four hexagrams—you do not know their names;
translations.idiomatic: of the sixty-four hexagrams you cannot name a single one;

sentences.zh: 莊子衆篇，何者內外；

translations.literal: among Zhuangzi's many chapters, which are inner and which outer;
translations.idiomatic: among Zhuangzi's many chapters, which are Inner, which Outer—

sentences.zh: 八袠所載，凡有幾家；

translations.literal: How many houses are recorded in the Eight Fascicles?
translations.idiomatic: How many schools are named in the Eight Fascicles?

sentences.zh: 《四本》之稱，以何爲長。

translations.literal: Of the title Four Roots, what does it excel in?
translations.idiomatic: Of the work called Four Roots, what is its strong point?

sentences.zh: 而終日欺人，人亦不受汝欺也。

translations.literal: Yet all day you deceive people—and people do not accept your deceit either.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you spend the day bluffing others, and others will not be bluffed by you either.

sentences.zh: 由吾不學，無以爲訓。

translations.literal: Because I did not study, I have nothing to offer as instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Because I never studied, I have nothing fit to pass on as teaching.

sentences.zh: 然重華無嚴父，放勳無令子，亦各由己耳。

translations.literal: Yet Chonghua had no strict father, and Fangxun had no worthy son—each bore it from himself alone.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Shun had no stern father, and Yao had no worthy son—each came to it by his own path.

sentences.zh: 汝輩竊議亦當云：「何日不學？

translations.literal: When you whisper among yourselves you surely say: 「Which day do we not study?
translations.idiomatic: When you mutter among yourselves you surely say: 「What day do we not study?

sentences.zh: 在天地閒可嬉戲，何忽自課謫？

translations.literal: Between heaven and earth one may sport—why suddenly impose penance on yourself?
translations.idiomatic: Under heaven and earth one may play—why suddenly set yourself a penance?

sentences.zh: 幸及盛時逐歲暮，何必有所減？

translations.literal: Luckily one reaches vigorous years chasing year's end—why must there be any cutback?
translations.idiomatic: Luckily one catches vigorous years before old age—why must anything be cut back?

sentences.zh: 」汝見其一耳，不全爾也。

translations.literal: 」You see only one side of it—not the whole for you.
translations.idiomatic: 」You see one face of it—not the whole, and not for you.

sentences.zh: 設令吾學如馬、鄭，亦必甚勝；

translations.literal: Suppose I had studied like Ma and Zheng, I would surely have been much superior;
translations.idiomatic: Suppose I had studied like Ma and Zheng, I would surely have stood far above you;

sentences.zh: 復倍不如，今亦必大減。

translations.literal: and again, doubled and still inferior—even now I would surely be greatly diminished.
translations.idiomatic: and again, if doubled and still below them—even now I would surely be much the lesser.

sentences.zh: 致之有由，從身上來也。

translations.literal: There is a reason for this—it comes from the person himself.
translations.idiomatic: There is a cause for it, and it rises from the man himself.

sentences.zh: 汝今壯年，自懃數倍許勝，劣及吾耳。

translations.literal: You are now in vigorous years; if diligent, several times superior—only inferior to reaching my level.
translations.idiomatic: You are in your prime; be diligent and you may be several times the better—only short of matching me.

sentences.zh: 世中比例舉眼是，汝足知此，不復具言。

translations.literal: Such comparisons in the world are everywhere you look—you know this well enough, no need to detail.
translations.idiomatic: Such comparisons fill the world wherever you look—you know it well enough; I need not spell it out.

sentences.zh: 吾在世，雖乏德素，要復推排人閒數十許年，故是一舊物，人或以比數汝等耳。

translations.literal: While I live, though lacking virtue and plainness, I have nevertheless ranked among men for several decades, so I am an old specimen—people may compare you to me.
translations.idiomatic: While I live, though short on virtue and plain living, I have still ranked among men for several decades, so I am an old piece on the board—people may set you beside me for measure.

sentences.zh: 卽化之後，若自無調度，誰復知汝事者？

translations.literal: After I am gone, if you have no self-discipline, who will know your affairs?
translations.idiomatic: Once I am gone, if you cannot govern yourselves, who will know your business?

sentences.zh: 舍中亦有少負令譽弱冠越超清級者，于時王家門中，優者則龍鳳，劣者猶虎豹，失蔭之後，豈龍虎之議？

translations.literal: In the clan there are also a few who in their prime bore fine reputation and leapt past clear ranks—in the Wang house then, the best were dragon and phoenix, the lesser still tiger and leopard—after losing their shelter, would one still speak of dragon and tiger?
translations.idiomatic: In the household there were also a few who in their prime won fair name and shot past the clear grades—in the Wang line then, the best were dragon and phoenix, the lesser still tiger and leopard; once the shade was gone, who still spoke of dragon and tiger?

sentences.zh: 況吾不能爲汝蔭，政應各自努力耳。

translations.literal: How much more when I cannot shelter you—you should each strive on your own.
translations.idiomatic: How much more when I cannot shade you—you must each drive yourselves.

sentences.zh: 或有身經三公，蔑爾無聞；

translations.literal: Some who passed through the Three Dukes are ignored as if nothing;
translations.idiomatic: Some who sat in the Three Excellencies are passed over as if they never were;

sentences.zh: 布衣寒素，卿相屈體。

translations.literal: some in plain cloth and cold poverty make ministers bow.
translations.idiomatic: some in hemp and cold poverty make ministers bow their bodies.

sentences.zh: 或父子貴賤殊，兄弟聲名異。

translations.literal: Some father and son differ in rank, brothers differ in fame.
translations.idiomatic: Some father and son stand far apart in rank, brothers far apart in name.

sentences.zh: 何也？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 體盡讀數百卷書耳。

translations.literal: Simply because they have thoroughly read several hundred scrolls of books.
translations.idiomatic: Simply because they have worn their way through several hundred scrolls of books.

sentences.zh: 吾今悔無所及，欲以前車誡爾後乘也。

translations.literal: My regret now cannot be mended—I wish to warn your cart behind by the cart that overturned ahead.
translations.idiomatic: My regret cannot be mended now—I mean to warn the cart behind with the cart that overturned ahead.

sentences.zh: 汝年入立境，方應從官，兼有室累，牽役情性，何處復得下帷如王郎時邪？

translations.literal: Your years enter the established stage, you should take office, and you have household burdens—what drags temperament—where could you again lower the curtain and study as in Lord Wang's day?
translations.idiomatic: Your years enter the standing of manhood, office awaits you, and household cares tug at your temper—where could you again lower the curtain and study as in the young Wang's day?

sentences.zh: 爲可作世中學，取過一生耳。

translations.literal: You can study what the world offers and scrape through life.
translations.idiomatic: You may take what learning the world allows and scrape through a life.

sentences.zh: 試復三思，勿諱吾言。

translations.literal: Try thinking again—do not dodge my words.
translations.idiomatic: Think it over again—do not dodge what I say.

sentences.zh: 猶捶撻志輩，冀脫万一，未死之閒，望有成就者，不知當有益否？

translations.literal: I still beat and urge those with will, hoping one in ten thousand escapes—before death, hoping for some achievement—do not know if it will help.
translations.idiomatic: I still lash and goad those who have will, hoping one in ten thousand may break free—before death, hoping for some mark—whether it will help, I do not know.

sentences.zh: 各在爾身己切，豈復關吾邪？

translations.literal: Each lies in your own person, already urgent—what does it have to do with me?
translations.idiomatic: Each rests in your own person, already pressing—what has that to do with me?

sentences.zh: 鬼唯知愛深松茂柏，寧知子弟毀譽事！

translations.literal: Ghosts only know to love deep pines and lush cypress—how would they know children's ruin and renown!
translations.idiomatic: Ghosts love only deep pine and thick cypress—how should they know sons and grandsons, ruin and renown!

sentences.zh: 因汝有感，故略敘胷懷矣。

translations.literal: Moved by you, I have sketched my inmost feelings.
translations.idiomatic: Stirred by you, I have sketched what lies in my breast.

sentences.zh: 張緒字思曼，吳郡吳人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Xu, styled Siman, was a native of Wu in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xu, styled Siman, came from Wu in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖茂度，會稽太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Maodu was administrator of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Maodu had been administrator of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 父寅，太子中舍人。

translations.literal: His father Yin was crown prince attendant within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yin had been crown prince attendant within the palace.

sentences.zh: 緒少知名，清簡寡欲，叔父鏡謂人曰：「此兒，今之樂廣也。」

translations.literal: Xu was known from youth, pure and spare, few desires; his uncle Jing told people: 「This boy is today's Yue Guang.」
translations.idiomatic: Xu was famed from youth, pure and spare, with few wants; his uncle Jing told others: 「This boy is the Yue Guang of our day.」

sentences.zh: 州辟議曹從事，舉秀才。

translations.literal: The province recruited him as aide in the deliberation bureau; he was nominated as eminent scholar.
translations.idiomatic: The province drafted him as aide in the deliberation bureau and nominated him as eminent scholar.

sentences.zh: 建平王護軍主簿，右軍法曹行參軍，司空主簿，撫軍、南中郎二府功曹，尚書倉部郎。

translations.literal: Chief clerk on Prince of Jianping's Army Protector staff, acting aide in the law bureau of the Right Army, chief clerk to the minister of works, merit recorder on the Pacification Army and Southern Central Staffs, gentleman of the ministry granary bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He served as chief clerk on Prince of Jianping's army-protector staff, acting aide in the Right Army law bureau, chief clerk to the minister of works, merit recorder on the pacification and southern central staffs, and gentleman of the ministry granary bureau.

sentences.zh: 都令史諮郡縣米事，緒蕭然直視，不以經懷。

translations.literal: Capital clerks consulted on county grain affairs; Xu looked straight ahead coolly, not taking it to heart.
translations.idiomatic: Capital clerks came to consult on county grain matters; Xu gazed off with cool detachment and never took it to heart.

sentences.zh: 除巴陵王文學，太子洗馬，北中郎參軍，太子中舍人，本郡中正，車騎從事中郎，中書郎，州治中，黃門郎。

translations.literal: He was made literary aide to the Prince of Baling, crown prince groom, northern central staff aide, crown prince attendant within the palace, chief rectifier of his native commandery, attendant of the chariot and horse staff, gentleman of the secretariat, commandery rectifier, gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was made literary aide to the Prince of Baling, crown prince groom, northern central staff aide, crown prince attendant within the palace, chief rectifier of his native commandery, attendant on the chariot and horse staff, secretariat gentleman, commandery rectifier, and gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 宋明帝每見緒，輙歎其清淡。

translations.literal: Whenever Emperor Ming of Song saw Xu he always praised his purity.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Emperor Ming of Song saw Xu he would sigh over his spare purity.

sentences.zh: 轉太子中庶子，本州大中正，遷司徒左長史。

translations.literal: He was moved to crown prince senior aide, grand rectifier of his native province, and shifted to left chief aide on the minister of education's staff.
translations.idiomatic: He became crown prince senior aide and grand rectifier of his native province, then shifted to left chief aide on the minister of education's staff.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書袁粲言於帝曰：「臣觀張緒有正始遺風，宜爲宮職。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Yuan Can said to the emperor: 「In my view Zhang Xu bears the legacy of the Zhengshi era and is fit for palace office.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of personnel Yuan Can told the emperor: 「I see in Zhang Xu the air of the Zhengshi masters; he is fit for palace rank.

sentences.zh: 」復轉中庶子，領翊軍校尉，轉散騎常侍，領長水校尉，尋兼侍中，遷吏部郎，參掌大選。

translations.literal: 」He was again made senior crown prince aide and held the colonelcy of the assisting army; he became regular attendant and held the colonelcy of the long river; soon he also served as attendant, was moved to director of the ministry of personnel, and shared charge of the great selection.
translations.idiomatic: 」He was again made senior crown prince aide and held the colonelcy of the assisting army; he became regular attendant and held the long river colonelcy; before long he also served as attendant, was moved to director of the ministry of personnel, and shared charge of the great selection.

sentences.zh: 元徽初，東宮罷，選曹擬舍人王儉格外記室，緒以儉人地兼美，宜轉祕書丞，從之。

translations.literal: At the opening of Yuanhui the eastern palace was abolished; the selection bureau proposed Registrar Wang Jian as extraordinary recorder outside the ranks; Xu held that Jian's person and standing were both fine and he should be shifted to secretariat aide—the proposal was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Yuanhui the eastern palace was shut; the selection bureau proposed Registrar Wang Jian as extraordinary recorder outside the ranks; Xu argued that Jian's person and standing were both excellent and he should be shifted to secretariat aide—the throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 緒又遷侍中，郎如故。

translations.literal: Xu was again moved to attendant; his directorate stood as before.
translations.idiomatic: Xu was again made attendant, while keeping his directorate.

sentences.zh: 緒忘情榮祿，朝野皆貴其風，嘗與客閑言，一生不解作諾。
