translations.literal: Xu put rank and stipend out of mind; court and countryside alike prized his air; he once said to guests in idle talk that in his whole life he never learned to say yes.
translations.idiomatic: Xu set rank and stipend out of mind; court and countryside alike honored his bearing; chatting once with guests, he said he had never in his life learned to say yes.

sentences.zh: 時袁粲、褚淵秉政，有人以緒言告粲、淵者，卽出緒爲吳郡太守，緒初不知也。

translations.literal: At the time Yuan Can and Chu Yuan held power; someone reported Xu's words to Can and Yuan, and at once Xu was sent out as administrator of Wu commandery—at first he did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Can and Chu Yuan then held the reins; someone carried Xu's remark to Can and Yuan, and at once he was sent out as administrator of Wu commandery—at first he did not know it.

sentences.zh: 遷爲祠部尚書，復領中正，遷太常，加散騎常侍，尋領始安王師。

translations.literal: He was moved to minister of rites for the imperial clan, again held the chief rectifiercy, was moved to grand minister of ceremonies, was given added rank as regular attendant, and soon held tutor to the Prince of Shi'an.
translations.idiomatic: He became minister of rites for the imperial clan, again held the chief rectifiercy, was moved to grand minister of ceremonies, was given added rank as regular attendant, and soon tutored the Prince of Shi'an.

sentences.zh: 昇明二年，遷太祖太傅長史，加征虜將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shengming he was moved to chief aide on the Grand Ancestor's grand tutor staff, with added rank as general who chastises the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shengming he became chief aide on the Grand Ancestor's grand tutor staff, with added rank as general who chastises the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 尋加驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was given added rank as valiant cavalry general.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was given added rank as valiant cavalry general.

sentences.zh: 欲用緒爲右僕射，以問王儉，儉曰：「南士由來少居此職。

translations.literal: They wished to appoint Xu Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and asked Wang Jian; Jian said: 「Southerners from of old have seldom held this office.
translations.idiomatic: They meant to make Xu Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and consulted Wang Jian; Jian said, 「Men of the south have rarely held this post.

sentences.zh: 」褚淵在座，啟上曰：「儉年少，或不盡憶。

translations.literal: 」Chu Yuan was present and reported to the throne: 「Jian is young and may not remember everything.
translations.idiomatic: 」Chu Yuan, who was in attendance, told the throne, 「Jian is still young and may not recall the full record.

sentences.zh: 江左用陸玩、顧和，皆南人也。

translations.literal: Under Jiangzuo, Lu Wan and Gu He were both employed—and both were southerners.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiangzuo era Lu Wan and Gu He were both appointed—and both were men of the south.

sentences.zh: 」儉曰：「晉氏衰政，不可以爲准則。

translations.literal: 」Jian said: 「The Jin house's decadent governance cannot serve as a standard.
translations.idiomatic: 」Jian replied, 「The Jin dynasty's corrupt rule cannot be taken as a model.

sentences.zh: 」上乃止。

translations.literal: 」The emperor then dropped the matter.
translations.idiomatic: 」The emperor thereupon abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 四年，初立國學，以緒爲太常卿，領國子祭酒，常侍、中正如故。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the National Academy was first established; Xu was made Director of Ceremonies, concurrent Director of the Imperial University; regular attendant and rectifier of the third rank as before.
translations.idiomatic: In year four the National Academy was founded; Xu was made director of ceremonies with concurrent charge as director of the imperial university, his posts as regular attendant and rectifier unchanged.

sentences.zh: 緒旣遷官，上以王延之代緒爲中書令，時人以此選爲得人，比晉朝之用王子敬、王季琰也。

translations.literal: Once Xu had moved office, the emperor had Wang Yanzhi replace him as Director of the Secretariat; men of the time held this choice a fit appointment, likening it to the Jin court's use of Wang Zijing and Wang Jiyan.
translations.idiomatic: After Xu's transfer the emperor set Wang Yanzhi in his place as director of the secretariat; contemporaries called the pick a happy one, comparing it to the Jin dynasty's pairing of Wang Zijing and Wang Jiyan.

sentences.zh: 緒長於《周易》，言精理奧，見宗一時。

translations.literal: Xu excelled in the Book of Changes; his discourse was refined and its principles profound, and he was honored for a time.
translations.idiomatic: Xu was master of the Book of Changes—his speech subtle and its principles deep—and for a season the age looked up to him.

sentences.zh: 常云何平叔所不解《易》中七事，諸卦中所有時義，是其一也。

translations.literal: He would often say that among the seven matters in the Changes He Yan could not grasp, the timely meanings found in the various hexagrams were one.
translations.idiomatic: He often remarked that of the seven points in the Changes He Yan could not fathom, the timely import within each hexagram was one of them.

sentences.zh: 緒口不言利，有財輙散之。

translations.literal: Xu never spoke of profit; whenever he had wealth he gave it away.
translations.idiomatic: Xu would not speak of gain; the moment money came to hand he scattered it.

sentences.zh: 清言端坐，或竟日無食，門生見緒飢，爲之辨餐，然未嘗求也。

translations.literal: He would sit in pure discourse; sometimes he went a whole day without food. When disciples saw Xu hungry they prepared meals for him, yet he never asked.
translations.idiomatic: He sat in quiet talk for hours; at times he ate nothing all day. When students saw him famished they laid out food for him, but he never once begged for it.

sentences.zh: 卒時年六十八。

translations.literal: When he died he was sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 遺命作蘆葭轜車，靈上置杯水香火，不設祭。

translations.literal: His final instruction was a reed-lined funeral bier; on the bier only a cup of water and incense—no sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: By his own order his coffin was a cart lined with reeds; on the spirit stand only a cup of water and incense—no offerings.

sentences.zh: 從弟融敬重緒，事之如親兄，齎酒於緒靈前酌飲，慟哭曰：「阿兄風流頓盡！

translations.literal: His cousin Rong revered Xu and treated him like an elder brother; he brought wine and drank before Xu's spirit, wailing: 「Elder brother—your grace is utterly gone!
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Rong honored Xu and served him as he would an elder brother; he carried wine, poured a libation before Xu's spirit, and wept aloud: 「Brother—your elegance is spent!

sentences.zh: 」追贈散騎常侍、特進、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: 」Posthumously he was given Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Special Advancement, and Household Minister with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: 」After death he was granted regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, special advancement, and household minister with the golden seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 諡簡子。

translations.literal: Posthumous title: Master Simple.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Jianzi, Master Simple.

sentences.zh: 子克，蒼梧世，正員郎，險行見寵，坐廢錮。

translations.literal: His son Ke, under the Cangwu emperor, was a regular secretariat gentleman; his reckless conduct won favor, and for it he was stripped and confined.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ke, in the Cangwu reign, held a regular secretariat post; his rash ways pleased the throne until he was disgraced and put under confinement.

sentences.zh: 克弟允，永明中，安西功曹，淫通殺人，伏法。

translations.literal: Ke's younger brother Yun, in Yongming, was staff officer on the Pacify-the-West command; he committed adultery and murder and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Ke's younger brother Yun, in Yongming, served as staff officer to the Pacify-the-West general; he lay with another man's wife and killed a man, and paid with his life.

sentences.zh: 允兄充，永明元年，爲武陵王友，坐書與尚書令王儉，辭旨激揚，爲御史中丞到撝所奏，免官禁錮。

translations.literal: Yun's elder brother Chong, in Yongming year 1, was friend to the Prince of Wuling; he was charged for a letter to Director of the Secretariat Wang Jian with heated language, reported by Censor-in-Chief Dao Hu, and was dismissed and confined.
translations.idiomatic: Yun's elder brother Chong, in Yongming year 1, was companion to the Prince of Wuling; he wrote Wang Jian, director of the secretariat, in words sharp and provocative, was impeached by censor-in-chief Dao Hu, and was removed from office and forbidden to serve.

sentences.zh: 論者以爲有恨於儉也。

translations.literal: Commentators thought he bore a grudge against Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Opinion held that he nursed a grievance against Jian.

sentences.zh: 案建元初，中詔序朝臣，欲以右僕射擬張岱。

translations.literal: Note: Early in Jianyuan, an inner edict ranked court ministers and would have matched Zhang Dai to Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial note: At the opening of Jianyuan an inner edict ordered the ranking of ministers and would have set Zhang Dai as Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 褚淵謂「得此過優，若別有忠誠，特進升引者，別是一理，仰由裁照」。

translations.literal: Chu Yuan said, 「This rank is too generous; if there is separate loyalty warranting special advancement and promotion, that is another matter—defer to Your judgment.」
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yuan said, 「The appointment is too lofty; if some other loyalty merits special advancement, that is a different case—let Your Majesty decide.」

sentences.zh: 詔「更量」。

translations.literal: The edict said, 「Weigh again.」
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied, 「Reconsider.」

sentences.zh: 說者旣異，今兩記焉。

translations.literal: The accounts differ; both are recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: The tellings diverge; both are set down here.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：王僧虔有希聲之量，兼以藝業。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Wang Sengqian possessed the measure of rare renown, together with mastery of the arts.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Wang Sengqian had the stature of sound too faint to hear, joined to mastery of his craft.

sentences.zh: 戒盈守滿，屈己自容，方軌諸公，實平世之良相。

translations.literal: He guarded against excess and held to fullness, bent himself to get along, matched the grandees in measure—a true worthy minister in an age of peace.
translations.idiomatic: He shunned overflow and kept to the full, bowed himself to fit the room, stood level with the great lords, and was in truth a fine minister for a tranquil age.

sentences.zh: 張緒凝衿素氣，自然標格，搢紳端委，朝宗民望。

translations.literal: Zhang Xu had a gathered bearing and plain spirit, a natural nobility; girdled-clan dignitaries in formal dress were the court's hope and the people's gaze.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xu bore a concentrated purity and an unadorned air, a nobility that came of itself; belted officials in court dress were what the age looked to and the people watched.

sentences.zh: 夫如緒之風流者，豈不謂之名臣！

translations.literal: One such as Xu's grace—who would not call him a famed minister!
translations.idiomatic: A man of Xu's elegance—who would not name him a great minister!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：簡穆長者，其義恢恢。

translations.literal: The encomium says: the elder of Jianmu—his principle is vast.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium runs: Jianmu's elder lord—his meaning wide and high.

sentences.zh: 聲律草隷，燮理三台。

translations.literal: Tone and rhythm, draft and clerical script; he harmonized the Three Platforms.
translations.idiomatic: Music's laws and grass and clerical hands; he tuned the Three Platforms.

sentences.zh: 思曼廉靜，自絕風埃。

translations.literal: Siman was pure and still, cutting himself off from worldly dust.
translations.idiomatic: Siman lived in clean quiet, severing himself from the world's grime.

sentences.zh: 遊心《爻繫》，物允清才。

translations.literal: His mind roamed the Commentary on the Judgments and Images; all agreed he was clear talent.
translations.idiomatic: His heart ranged through the Judgments and Images; men allowed he was bright talent.

translations.idiomatic: [1] Endnote marker.
